questions.q:
Paper 1 prints the area of study above each extract. State the number and name of the area of study for each of these extracts:
(a) a nuevo tango by Piazzolla
(b) part of a ballet score
(c) a performance by an Arab takht ensemble
ms: (b) Area 7: Music for stage and screen
Accept the name without the number, or the number without the name
questions.model: (a) Area 5, Music for dance. (b) Area 7, Music for stage and screen. (c) Area 6, Music for small ensemble.
questions.tip: Ballet counts as stage music (Area 7), even though people dance to it.

questions.q: Apart from following a printed score, state two things Paper 1 may ask you to do with printed music.
ms: transpose a short passage to concert pitch
choose the missing melody or rhythm from options
questions.model: Identify the key of the passage, and transpose a passage for a transposing instrument to concert pitch.

questions.q:
A student hears an extract labelled 'Area of study 1: Baroque' (a fast concerto grosso movement) and writes:
"The music is fast and loud and sounds happy, with lots of instruments."
Rewrite this as a 4-mark answer, replacing each vague idea with a precise musical term or feature.
ms: fast → allegro / fast tempo with a steady driving pulse
loud → forte, with terraced dynamics (sudden changes, e.g. tutti loud, concertino quieter)
lots of instruments → concertino and ripieno (tutti) strings
any other accurate Baroque feature, e.g. ritornello, imitation, sequences
questions.model: The tempo is allegro with a driving, constant pulse. The dynamics are terraced: loud tutti passages for the ripieno contrast suddenly with quieter passages for the concertino. The music is in a major key, and a harpsichord continuo plays the chords under the bass line.
questions.tip: Marks go to specific terms. 'Fast', 'loud' and 'happy' on their own score nothing.

questions.q:
An extract is described like this: "A small group of musicians sit on a low platform. A short-necked, fretless lute and a plucked zither play an ornamented melody that uses notes between the semitones, with a goblet-shaped drum and a tambourine."
(a) Name the area of study and the tradition. [2]
(b) Name the lute and the zither. [2]
questions.model: (a) Area 6, Music for small ensemble: an Arab takht ensemble. (b) The lute is the oud and the zither is the qanun.
questions.tip: Notes between the semitones = quarter-tones, a strong clue for maqām-based music.

questions.q:
Paper 1 has one short descriptive question. An extract labelled 'Area of study 3: Romantic' is described like this:
"It begins very quietly. The cellos and basses hold one low note (the key note) for many bars while the chords above change. A solo horn plays a long, expressive melody with wide leaps; the player slows down and speeds up freely. The full orchestra then gets gradually louder to a very loud climax with cymbal crashes, before the music suddenly becomes very quiet. The key is minor and there are many notes outside the key."
Write a descriptive answer that names each feature with the correct musical term.
ms: tonic pedal (held bass note) in cellos and double basses
lyrical / expressive horn melody with a wide range and leaps (disjunct)
crescendo to a fortissimo / ff climax (tutti)
subito piano / sudden drop to pp
chromatic harmony (notes outside the key) / dissonance
large Romantic orchestra with expanded percussion (cymbals)
1 mark per correctly named feature, max 6
questions.model: The extract begins pianissimo with a tonic pedal in the cellos and double basses. A solo horn plays a lyrical, disjunct melody with a wide range, using rubato. A long crescendo leads to a fortissimo tutti climax with cymbals, followed by a sudden drop to piano. The tonality is minor and the harmony is chromatic, typical of a large Romantic orchestra.
questions.tip: Use the checklist M-H-R-T-S-D-I so you do not forget a whole element.

questions.q:
Cambridge IGCSE Music weights the components: Paper 1 Listening 40% (out of 70), Component 2 Performing 30% (out of 50), Component 3 Composing 30% (out of 50).
A student scores 49/70 in Listening, 38/50 in Performing and 30/50 in Composing.
(a) Calculate the student's overall weighted percentage. [4]
(b) The student could gain 5 more raw marks in one component. Which component gives the biggest gain in weighted percentage? Show your working. [2]
ms: (b) M1: 5/70 × 40 ≈ 2.86% for Listening vs 5/50 × 30 = 3% for Performing or Composing
(b) A1: Performing or Composing (each worth 3%), slightly more than Listening
questions.model:
(a) Listening 49/70 × 40 = 28; Performing 38/50 × 30 = 22.8; Composing 30/50 × 30 = 18. Total = 68.8%.
(b) In Listening 5 marks = 5/70 × 40 ≈ 2.86%; in Performing or Composing 5 marks = 5/50 × 30 = 3%. So 5 marks in Performing or Composing is worth slightly more.
questions.tip: Coursework is 60% of the grade: each raw mark there is worth 0.6%, compared with about 0.57% in Listening.
